It is worth noting that the precipitates are mainly Fe2Nb particles proved by the selected area diffraction pattern of high magnification TEM in our previous study [22].

The recrystallization temperature increases with the increasing of Nb contents. For example, a high annealing temperature of 1100 °C cannot realize a fully recrystallization process in FeCrAlMo alloys as shown in Fig. 7(i) when the Nb contents increases to 1.5 wt%.
Hence it can be concluded that P2 peak is related to the recovery of dislocations produced by the cold rolling process and recrystallization during the heat process.
Here it is worth to note that the appearance of P3 peak indicates that the grain boundaries can move freely and have not been pinned by any precipitation particles.

For example, the UTS of FeCrAlMo alloy with 1.5 wt% Nb corresponding to different annealing temperature of 800 °C, 900 °C, 1000 °C and 1100 °C is 628 MPa, 562 MPa, 692 MPa and 466 MPa, which is 44.0%, 27.7%, 48.2% and 20.0% higher than that of Nb-free FeCrAlMo alloy with the same annealing temperature, respectively.

For example, UTS of N15 1000 alloys at RT, 300 °C, 500 °C and 800 °C are about 692 MPa, 510 MPa, 470 MPa and 95 MPa, which are 48.5%, 45.7%, 27.0% and 58.3% higher than that of N0 1000 alloys at the same test temperature, respectively.

mechanisms.name: pinning effect of Fe2Nb particles on dislocations and grain boundaries

evidence.quote: the disappearance of P2 (recrystallization peak) and P3 (grain boundary peak) in the Nb containing FeCrAlMo alloys well proved that this pinning effect by high density Fe2Nb nanoscale particles was the main reason for improving the tensile strength of the Nb containing FeCrAlMo alloys.

The recrystallization temperature increases with the increasing of Nb contents. For example, a high annealing temperature of 1100 °C cannot realize a fully recrystallization process in FeCrAlMo alloys as shown in Fig. 7(i) when the Nb contents increases to 1.5 wt%.
Based on the optical micrographs analysis, the reason may be the pinning effect by the high density nanoscale Fe2Nb particles on dislocations, P2 peak would be expected to find at higher temperature
